editor.label: Python code editor
editor.timeout: Your code took too long (maybe an endless loop?). Python was restarted.
editor.loadError: Python couldn’t start. Check your internet connection and press Run again.

errors.SyntaxError: Python couldn’t read a line. Check for a missing quote, parenthesis or colon.
errors.IndentationError: The spaces at the start of a line don’t line up. Python uses indentation to group code.
errors.NameError: You used a name Python doesn’t know yet. Check the spelling, or create the variable first.
errors.TypeError: You mixed types that don’t work together, like adding text and a number. Try str() or int().
errors.ValueError: The type is right but the value isn’t, like int("hello").
errors.ZeroDivisionError: You divided by zero. Even Python can’t do that!
errors.IndexError: You asked for a position that doesn’t exist in the list. Remember: counting starts at 0.
errors.KeyError: That key isn’t in the dictionary. Check the spelling.
errors.AttributeError: That value doesn’t have the method or property you used. Check the spelling.
errors.EOFError: Your code asked for input(), but there was nothing to read.
errors.generic: Read the last line of the error. It names the problem and the line number.

terms.title: Before you start
terms.body:
Python Quest follows the topic order of **30 Days Of Python**, a free repository on GitHub by Asabeneh Yetayeh. Python Quest is an independent project. That author did not create, review or endorse it.

The original repository doesn’t include a license, so its author keeps the rights to its text, code and images.

By continuing, you agree that:

- You use this app, and any content taken from or based on the 30 Days Of Python repository, **under your own personal responsibility**.
- You’ll use it for personal learning only, and you won’t copy, publish or sell material from the original repository without its author’s permission.
- If you want to use the original material for anything else, you’ll ask its author first.
